Details: EarthSignal
Baseline Product Specification v1.0
Planning only; no coding started

An interactive environmental intelligence platform for exploring Indian cities as evolving digital worlds, discovering environmental changes, testing carefully defined scenarios, and inspecting the evidence behind every result.
A navigable 3D Earth transitions into city terrain, satellite imagery, environmental layers, and neighbourhood-level analysis.
The globe should make users curious; scientifically trustworthy results should make them stay.
Make environmental change understandable through interactive exploration.
Compare places and years using traceable data.
Detect unusual changes without confusing statistical anomalies with proven environmental damage.
Provide forecasts and hypothetical scenarios with uncertainty clearly communicated.
Make analysis inspectable and reproducible.
Demonstrate serious engineering and data-science skills in a portfolio-quality application.
Not a replacement for Google Maps or a live navigation service.
Not a real-time digital twin of every building or environmental process.
Does not prove causation from correlation alone.
Not an AI chatbot that invents environmental facts.
Does not promise exact knowledge of a city's future.
All audiences: curious citizens, students, researchers, environmental scientists, urban planners, NGOs, and decision-makers.
India-wide architecture, with one pilot city validated first.
Chandigarh, subject to data availability, boundary validation, historical coverage, and processing feasibility.
Investigate changes, predict future trends where valid, and compare carefully defined hypothetical interventions.
Earth: immersive 3D globe, city search, environmental highlights.
City: satellite imagery, boundaries, and environmental map layers.
Investigation: timelines, comparisons, anomalies, and evidence.
Experiment: validated models, scenario assumptions, and uncertainty.

Candidate: Copernicus Sentinel-2. Calculate vegetation indices and compare relatively fine-grained patterns; band resolutions vary.
Candidate: USGS Landsat Collection 2. Historical observations extend back decades; scene quality, sensor differences, and cloud cover require screening.
Candidates: ERA5 and ERA5-Land. Provide atmospheric context at coarser spatial resolution than satellite vegetation layers.
Candidate: CPCB monitoring data. Validate historical coverage, station quality, access conditions, and permissions.
Official municipal/government geospatial sources; OpenStreetMap may supplement if licence and suitability are checked.
For each dataset record source, licence, temporal coverage, spatial resolution, processing history, quality flags, and update policy.
Record source version, processing parameters, code version, and processing date for each run.
Do not promise a uniform 20-year record for every variable. Sentinel-2 starts in 2017; Landsat, ERA5, and air-quality records have different coverage and resolutions.
Do not imply neighbourhood-level precision for coarse weather grids or sparse air-quality stations. Display actual measurement resolution.
Ingest source data and run quality checks.
Standardise units, dates, coordinates, and metadata.
Apply cloud, missing-data, and quality masks.
Perform spatial and temporal aggregation.
Store versioned analysis-ready raster and vector datasets.
Serve maps, charts, comparisons, anomaly analysis, forecasts, and scenario experiments.
Attach evidence and source information to each finding.
Calculate NDVI = (NIR - Red) / (NIR + Red) from suitable reflectance bands. Mask clouds and shadows; aggregate comparable seasonal or annual periods; report valid-pixel coverage.
NDVI indicates vegetation greenness; it is not a direct measure of tree count, biodiversity, or total green space.
Use quality-screened Landsat surface-temperature products; apply scale factors and masks; compare consistent seasonal windows; report units and observation counts.
Land-surface temperature is not the same as air temperature or the temperature experienced by people.
Compare consistent geographic units and periods; calculate median NDVI, temperature, changes, valid-pixel coverage, observation counts, weather context, and available station readings.
Do not present areas with missing observations as healthy or unchanged; expose data gaps and quality.
Start with explainable statistical methods and robust seasonal baselines. A z-score may be used where assumptions fit; consider autocorrelation, skew, multiple testing, and minimum sample counts.
An anomaly is unusual relative to a defined baseline; it does not automatically indicate harm or establish a cause.
Train on past data and evaluate future periods using chronological holdouts and rolling-origin backtesting.
Keep hypothetical interventions separate from forecasts. Define changed variables, fixed assumptions, applicability, and evidence before interpreting outputs.
Compare each model against a simple baseline.
Split data chronologically and prevent future information from entering training.
Where feasible, evaluate on unseen geographic areas as well as held-out periods.
Use suitable metrics such as MAE and RMSE; evaluate uncertainty interval calibration and coverage.
Record training data, features, model version, parameters, and limitations.
Do not issue a prediction when data quality or model applicability is inadequate.

Real-time global monitoring, complete histories for every Indian city, building-level temperature, unsupported causal claims, complex multi-agent AI, social features, and expensive cloud infrastructure.

3–5 weeks estimated. Build ingestion, masks, summaries, aggregation, metadata, and reproducible processing. Exit: validated outputs and automated tests.
3–5 weeks estimated. Build globe, city transition, map layers, timeline, and responsive panels. Exit: actual processed data is explorable.
2–4 weeks estimated. Add comparisons, anomalies, evidence views, and one story. Exit: user can reproduce and understand a finding.
3–5 weeks estimated. Evaluate one forecasting model; add scenario comparisons only if assumptions and data support them.
2–4 weeks estimated. Polish animations, add evidence-backed AI, reports, deployment, and documentation.
Approximately 14–25 weeks as a planning range; re-estimate after Phase 0. A beginner learning during development may need longer.

A user can open the deployed site, navigate to the pilot city, explore real historical data, compare areas and years, investigate a change, inspect evidence, and examine one properly evaluated prediction.
Build a virtual world that looks extraordinary because the science inside it is extraordinary—not because animation is hiding an ordinary project.
